skill.name: happyhorse-1-0
skill.description: Guides text-to-video generation with HappyHorse 1.0 through the RunComfy CLI. It documents supported parameters, prompt patterns, output behavior, and when to use related video models.
skill.summary: Generate HappyHorse 1.0 text-to-video clips through RunComfy with structured prompt and CLI guidance.
skill.author: runcomfy-com

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, fenced examples, and abbreviated HTTP paths. Confirmed residual risk is limited to intended RunComfy CLI execution and network submission of prompts and bearer-token-authenticated requests. A high-confidence semantic supply-chain issue remains because install instructions reference a different GitHub repository than the reviewed source metadata.

remediation.issue: Repository mismatch in public links and install command.
remediation.suggestion: Update the GitHub link and npx install command to the reviewed repository, or document a verified ownership relationship between both repositories.

remediation.issue: External RunComfy CLI execution is part of normal use.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npx, npm, runcomfy login, or runcomfy run commands from this skill.

remediation.issue: Prompts and bearer-token-authenticated requests are sent to RunComfy.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the external API submission clearly and avoid sending confidential prompts unless the user accepts that transfer.
Keep token files owner-only, prefer environment-scoped tokens in CI, and never print token file contents in generated instructions.

content.value_statement: Text-to-video setup can be unclear when model parameters, durations, and output settings differ. This skill guides HappyHorse 1.0 prompts and RunComfy CLI calls.
actual_capabilities: Documents the HappyHorse 1.0 text-to-video endpoint and RunComfy CLI invocation.
Lists supported input fields for prompt, aspect ratio, resolution, duration, seed, and watermark.
Provides sample commands for default, vertical, and lower-cost test generations.
Gives prompt guidance for motion, camera direction, multi-shot consistency, and audio cues.
Explains exit codes, API flow, token storage, and output download behavior.
Compares when to choose HappyHorse 1.0 instead of related video models.
limitations: Requires a RunComfy account, local CLI setup, valid authentication, and network access.
Covers the text-to-video endpoint only, not image-to-video generation.
Supports clips from 3 to 15 seconds and only the documented aspect ratios.
Install instructions should be verified because the skill references an external GitHub repository.

use_cases.title: Prototype Short Video Ads
use_cases.description: Create vertical or widescreen ad concepts with motion, camera direction, and synchronized ambience.

use_cases.title: Create Cinematic Concept Clips
use_cases.description: Draft short cinematic scenes with consistent characters, wardrobe anchors, and scene-specific sound direction.

use_cases.title: Test Video Prompts in Automation
use_cases.description: Run repeatable HappyHorse prompt trials with fixed parameters, seeds, and output folders.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Video Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a default HappyHorse generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use HappyHorse 1.0 to generate a 5 second 16:9 1080p video. Scene: [describe the motion, setting, and audio]. Save outputs to [folder].

prompt_templates.title: Vertical Social Short
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a mobile-first video with explicit output settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an 8 second 9:16 HappyHorse video without a watermark. Include camera movement, one clear action, and ambient audio. Scene: [details].

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Shot Character Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep a character consistent across two beats.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 10 second HappyHorse video with two shots. Keep [character, wardrobe, and prop] consistent in both shots, then describe how the action changes.

prompt_templates.title: Production Comparison Run
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt iteration with controlled variants.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three HappyHorse variants at 720P using seeds [seed list]. Keep the same prompt, compare the outputs, and recommend the best version for final 1080p generation.

output_examples.input: Generate a five second 16:9 clip of a runner crossing a rainy bridge.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares a HappyHorse 1.0 request using default 1080p resolution, five second duration, and a motion-focused prompt.

output_examples.input: Make a vertical cafe ad with no watermark and warm audio.
output_examples.output: The skill selects 9:16 format, disables the watermark, adds cafe ambience, and keeps the scene focused on one clear action.

output_examples.input: Explain why my request failed with a 30 second duration.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies a schema mismatch because HappyHorse supports 3 to 15 second clips and suggests splitting the scene.

best_practices: Describe motion over time with clear camera and audio cues.
Keep prompts under 2,500 characters and use only supported output settings.
Use 720P, short duration, and fixed seeds for early prompt tests.
anti_patterns: Using static image descriptions that do not explain movement.
Combining many unrelated actions or conflicting visual styles in one clip.
Sending external audio or image-to-video requirements to this text-only endpoint.

faq.question: Does this skill require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and valid authentication before generation can run.

faq.question: Which HappyHorse endpoint does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers the HappyHorse 1.0 text-to-video endpoint on RunComfy.

faq.question: Can it create audio with the video?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports in-pass audio direction through the prompt, but it does not accept external audio input.

faq.question: What clip lengths are supported?
faq.answer: The documented duration range is 3 to 15 seconds.

faq.question: Where are generated videos saved?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads generated outputs into the output directory selected for the run.

faq.question: What security review is needed before use?
faq.answer: Confirm the install source, approve RunComfy CLI execution, and expect prompts plus authentication to be sent to RunComfy.
